AMBIGUOUS describes a THING with more than one possible meaning. AMBIVALENT describes a PERSON with mixed feelings. | The ending is ambiguous; the reader is ambivalent. | Never say 'he was ambiguous about the offer'.
The speaker or text IMPLIES; the reader or listener INFERS. | Authors imply, you infer. | SAT loves this in 'what can be inferred' versus 'the author implies'.

SUBSTANTIATE means to supply evidence for a claim that had none. CORROBORATE means to ADD confirming evidence to something already claimed by another source. | You substantiate your own claim; a second study corroborates the first.

abate: PAIR - refute vs rebut vs repudiate
(v.) to lessen in intensity. The storm a: REFUTE means to actually PROVE false. REBUT means to argue against without necessarily proving. REPUDIATE means to disown or reject, often your own earlier view. | A rebuttal may fail; a refutation succeeds by definition.
SKEPTICAL means withholding belief pending evidence, which is a neutral scientific stance. CYNICAL means assuming bad motives. | Reviewers were skeptical of the data, not cynical about it.
NUANCE is a subtle distinction that ADDS precision. AMBIGUITY is a lack of clarity that SUBTRACTS it. | Nuance is a virtue; ambiguity is usually a flaw.
EXPLICIT is stated outright. IMPLICIT is present but unstated. | If the text says it, it is explicit; if you must supply it, it is implicit.
TANGENTIAL means only glancingly RELATED to the topic. PERIPHERAL means of minor IMPORTANCE, possibly still on-topic. | A tangential point wanders; a peripheral point is just small.
PRAGMATIC is practical and is a compliment. EXPEDIENT is convenient at the cost of principle and is a criticism. | Watch the connotation; the SAT tests it.
UNDERMINE means to WEAKEN gradually. REFUTE means to DEFEAT outright. | New data can undermine a theory long before anything refutes it.
CONCEDE means to admit a point. CONDONE means to approve of or overlook wrongdoing. | She conceded the error; she did not condone it.
AFFECT is almost always the VERB (to influence). EFFECT is almost always the NOUN (the result). | Rare exception: 'to effect change' means to bring it about.
The WHOLE comprises the parts; the PARTS compose the whole. | The archive comprises letters. The letters compose the archive. | 'Is comprised of' is the classic error.
PRESCRIBE means to recommend or order. PROSCRIBE means to FORBID. | Near-opposites separated by two letters, which is exactly why it appears.
DISCRETE means separate and distinct. DISCREET means tactful and private. | Three discrete categories; a discreet inquiry.
